title: The Field Where Fallen Seeds Remember Their Clouds

features.name: seed-ascending
features.desc-on-touch: A seed caught mid-fall, or mid-rise—you can't tell which direction it's moving. Above it, the memory of cloud. Below, the certainty of root.

features.name: cloud-genealogy
features.desc-on-touch: A chart pinned to a fencepost, listing the path from cloud to rain to soil to seed to plant. The arrows loop. Nothing here is linear.

features.name: root-reaching-memory
features.desc-on-touch: Beneath the visible soil, a root network spreads in a pattern that mirrors cloud-formation. The plant remembers the sky in its deepest growth.

features.name: fence-as-witness
features.desc-on-touch: Weathered posts mark the field boundary. Notches tally each seed that fell and rose. The fence has become a counter of impossible journeys.

features.name: agricultural-registry
features.desc-on-touch: A leather-bound book left open on a stump. Entries read like recipes at first: 'rain, soil, dark, waiting.' Then you realize it's accounting for metaphor instead of yield.

inscription: every fallen seed is a cloud remembering that it was once rain

file.name: Seed_Fall_Registry_Cross_Index_Cloudbase_Altitude_at_Moment_Release.txt
file.note: attempt to correlate when seeds leave plants with atmospheric pressure at that exact second. The data refuses pattern. Each seed fell at a different altitude in its own mind.

exits.label: back toward the chamber where seeds and rain were still ideas
toward the horizon where seed-memory becomes wind-carried
deeper into field, where rows end and forest begins
